summary.text: Lithification is the turning of loose, poorly consolidated sediment into sedimentary rock, an early part of the wider set of changes called diagenesis.
After deposition, sediments are compacted as later layers bury them and are cemented by minerals that precipitate from solution.
In the early stages pore space shrinks and water is squeezed out, while the sediment's main minerals stay unaltered.

facts.label: Two main steps
facts.value: Compaction under new layers and mineral cementing

facts.label: Early change
facts.value: Less pore space and water expelled

facts.label: Porosity trend
facts.value: Usually decreases, except in rare cases

items.prompt: Fresh mud settles on a lake floor and is slowly buried under more and more layers. What usually happens to the open spaces between its particles?

options.label: They grow as the mud dries
They fill with molten rock
They shrink as water is squeezed out
They stay exactly the same size

items.explain: As sediment turns to rock its porosity drops and water is expelled.

items.prompt: Besides being squeezed by the weight above, what binds loose sand grains into solid rock?

options.label: Minerals that precipitate from solution
Heat that melts the grains together
Plant roots that knit the grains
Ice that freezes between the grains

items.explain: Buried sediments are compacted and cemented by minerals that precipitate from solution.

items.prompt: Geologists separate diagenesis from metamorphism even though no sharp line divides them. What mainly sets metamorphism apart?

options.label: It happens only at the surface
It needs higher heat and pressure
It affects only fossils and bone
It always melts the rock fully

items.explain: There is no sharp boundary, but metamorphism takes place at higher temperatures and pressures than diagenesis.

items.prompt: A seashell buried in sediment is slowly swapped for a shiny iron mineral while keeping its shape. How can this happen?

options.label: Weathering at the surface adds iron
The shell melts and recools as metal
Erosion carves the shell into new shapes
Other minerals replace it during diagenesis

items.explain: During diagenesis, grains and fossils can be replaced by other minerals such as pyrite or marcasite.

items.prompt: Remains of plants and animals get buried in sediment and carried ever deeper. What can they eventually turn into?

options.label: Diamonds, through crushing pressure
Fresh water, as they dissolve
Kerogens and then hydrocarbons
Granite, as they harden

items.explain: Buried organic matter breaks down into kerogens and bitumens, and kerogens can later break down to form hydrocarbons.

items.prompt: Early in the change from soft clay sediment to rock, what happens to its main minerals?

options.label: They all melt and recrystallize
They mostly stay unaltered
They turn into new metamorphic minerals
They dissolve away completely

items.explain: In the early stages lithification is accompanied by lower porosity and water loss, while the main mineral assemblages remain unaltered.
